proof:
# An explicit all-cap OC center outside the failed selectors

Use the exact d=5 body and notation A,B,C,D,q,a from
`candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`. Define a point y
by its six barycentric coordinates in the standard middle simplex B:

    lambda_1=1/6-a/3,
    lambda_i=1/6+a/15 for i in {0,2,3,4,5}.             (1)

The positive coordinates sum to one. This is a single point of the actual
middle fiber. It is outside conv({g_B} union D), since

    (y_2-1/6)/(1/6-y_1)=1/5<9/2,

whereas every point of that hull with first coordinate below 1/6 has
the opposite inequality by its wedge constraint.

Every closed ambient halfspace containing (0,y) has at least the OC mass
for this fixed three-fiber body. Sections 1-3 prove the one-vertex cap
branches, including vertices on the boundary. Section 4 proves all other
branches using the signed-exponential comparison established in
`candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`.

This is an exact center certificate for the auxiliary selector-obstruction
example, not a general theorem for arbitrary mixed-integer convex bodies.
Its three fibers are full five-dimensional bodies, so the intrinsic
Hausdorff measure is H_5 and equals the sum of their five-dimensional
volumes; the common division by |B| in this note changes no inequality.

Write gamma=(5/6)^5 and tau=gamma(1+a/2), again in volume units |B|.
It suffices to consider caps whose boundary passes through y. In the
one-vertex case, let i be the strictly contained vertex, and let
ell_k in (0,1], k!=i, be the five intercept fractions on edges from i
to the other vertices. Then

    sum_(k!=i) lambda_k/ell_k=1,
    |B intersect H_0|/|B|=product_(k!=i)ell_k.

AM-GM on the five terms in the first display gives

    |B intersect H_0|/|B|>=5^5 product_(k!=i)lambda_k.   (2)

Equality is attainable at ell_k=5 lambda_k, which is <1 for the present
point. Formula (2) is only used in its proved one-vertex branch.

## 1. Type i=1 needs no endpoint contribution

Here (2) is

    gamma(1+(2/5)a)^5>=gamma(1+2a)>tau.

Thus every one-vertex cap of this type already exceeds the target on B.

## 2. Caps with a short edge intercept already have enough B mass

Suppose some ell_k<=7/10. Since a<10^(-5), all lambda_k are at least

    l=1/6-1/300000.

Put s=lambda_k/ell_k, so s>=s_0=l/(7/10)>1/5. Holding this one term
fixed, AM-GM bounds the product of all five terms by
s((1-s)/4)^4. This expression is decreasing for s>=1/5. Hence

 |B intersect H_0|/|B|
   >= l^5/[s_0((1-s_0)/4)^4]
   > gamma(1+1/200000)>=tau.                           (3)

The strict middle comparison is an exact rational inequality (its
left side is about 0.410284, while the right side is about 0.401880).
No approximation is used in the comparison.

## 3. All remaining one-vertex types have endpoint contribution exactly a

Now assume ell_k>=7/10 for every k!=i, with i!=1. Normalize the middle
affine cap margin as

    L(x)=1-sum_(k!=i)lambda_k(x)/ell_k.

For every x in B, L(x)>=-3/7. For each i in {0,2,3,4,5}, the simplex D
has a vertex w with lambda_i(w)>=T=3979/6000. At that vertex,

    L(w)>=1-(1-T)/(7/10)>1/2.

On the homothetic sub-simplex D'=(3/4)w+(1/4)D,

    L>= (3/4)(1/2)+(1/4)(-3/7)=15/56.

Write s=2-q. The exact volume bounds from the obstruction imply
q>20/11 and 0<s<2/11. Affineness of L and s+q=2 give

 min_(A)L + L(qx)
    =s min_(D)L +q L(x),        x in D.

For x in D' the right side is at least

    -(2/11)(3/7)+(20/11)(15/56)=9/22>0.                (4)

An arbitrary ambient cap with this middle trace has margin L(x)+vz.
If v<=min_A L, its entire A fiber is included, giving endpoint volume a.
If v>min_A L, (4) shows that its entire qD' sub-simplex in C is included.
That sub-simplex has relative volume 1/4^5=1/1024>a. Thus in every case
the endpoint contribution is at least a. Sending v sufficiently negative
isolates the whole A fiber, so its optimized value is exactly a.

Combining (2) with this endpoint contribution yields

 mu(H)/|B|>=gamma(1-2a)(1+(2/5)a)^4+a.

Using (1+(2/5)a)^4>=1+(8/5)a and 1-2a>0 gives a lower bound of

    gamma[1-(2/5)a-(16/5)a^2]+a.

Its excess above tau is at least

    a[1-(9/10)gamma-(16/5)gamma a]>0                  (5)

under a<=10^(-5), again by an exact rational comparison. This completes
the claimed certificate for all one-vertex middle traces, with arbitrary
integer tilts and all endpoint inclusion possibilities retained.

## 4. All multi-vertex branches from signed exponentials

The required scalar lemma is the following exact statement:

    If positive coefficients a_i,b_j satisfy sum_i a_i=sum_j b_j,
    and E_i,F_j are independent unit exponential variables, then

      P(sum_i a_i E_i >= sum_(j=1)^m b_j F_j)>=gamma_m.  (6)

It is proved in `candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`
by successively merging a smaller positive coefficient into a largest
one, which does not increase this probability. The final one-positive
value is product_j(1+b_j/sum_i a_i)^(-1), at least gamma_m by AM-GM.
The cited note gives the conditional-mean monotonicity, Stein identity,
density derivative sign, convolution derivative identity, and coefficient
limit proofs. Arbitrary positive-pair merging is NOT valid.

Let an ambient halfspace have its boundary through (0,y), and suppose its
middle trace strictly contains k>=2 vertices of B. Let its positive and
negative affine margins at B's vertices be a_i and -b_j respectively;
zero margins are omitted. Then k<=5 and 1<=m<=4. Put

    A_+=sum_i a_i, B_-=sum_j b_j,
    l=1/6-a/3, L=1/6+a/15.

Since the affine margin at y is zero and its barycentric coordinates
lie in [l,L],

    sum_i lambda_i a_i=sum_j lambda_j b_j,
    A_+/B_->=l/L.                                     (7)

Uniform volume in a simplex is represented by normalized independent
unit exponentials: their sum is independent of their normalized vector,
whose density is constant on the barycentric simplex. This follows
directly by the change of variables E_i=t lambda_i, whose Jacobian
is t^5. Consequently its cap-volume fraction is

    P(sum_i a_i E_i>=sum_j b_j F_j).                   (8)

If A_+>=B_-, scale the positive coefficients down to total B_-. This
only decreases the event, so (6) bounds (8) below by gamma_m.

If A_+<B_-, put r=B_-/A_+>1 and scale all k positive exponentials by r.
The resulting balanced probability is at least gamma_m by (6). The
density of the k-vector of scaled independent exponentials is

    r^(-k) exp(-sum x_i/r),       x_i>=0,

which pointwise dominates r^(-k) times their original density. Their
total variation distance is therefore at most 1-r^(-k). Keeping the
negative variables unchanged cannot increase this distance. It follows
that the unscaled probability (8) is at least

    gamma_m-[1-(A_+/B_-)^k]
       >=gamma_m-k(1-A_+/B_-)
       >=gamma_4-12a.                                 (9)

The last estimate uses k<=5, (7), and

    1-l/L=(12a/5)/(1+2a/5)<=12a/5.

The exact rational comparison

    gamma_4-12/100000
         >gamma_5(1+1/200000)                         (10)

and a<10^(-5) now prove that B ALONE supplies more than tau for every
multi-positive-vertex middle trace. This argument directly tracks the
actual point y; no unquantified perturbation of a centroid cap is used.

## 5. Completion for every closed ambient halfspace

Every nonvertical ambient cap containing (0,y) can be shrunk to a cap
through that point, without increasing its mass. Its middle trace properly
cuts B, since y is interior, and it has at least one strictly positive
and at least one strictly negative vertex margin. Sections 1-3 cover the
one-positive-vertex case; section 4 covers all other cases. A vertical
cap containing (0,y) contains all of B and therefore has relative mass
at least one, greater than tau. All endpoint tilts, boundary vertices,
and endpoint supporting coincidences have thus been retained.

Accordingly (1) is a single explicit point of S and an all-cap OC center
for this fixed example. This is only a concrete center for the auxiliary
counterexample family, not a general resolution of OC. It establishes
that the earlier selector obstruction is escaped by an actual point
outside its candidate hull, with no halfspace orientations omitted.
